record.original_question: For isotropic composites made from two isotropic elastic phases, with one phase possibly rigid or void, can one derive bounds on the achievable effective bulk and shear modulus pairs (kappa*,mu*) that improve on the current best-known inequalities, and ultimately determine the optimal bounds exactly?

evidence.quote: Problem 14: Can one obtain improved bounds on the elastic moduli pairs of isotropic composites of two isotropic elastic phases, and ultimately find the optimal ones?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider isotropic composite materials formed by mixing two isotropic linearly elastic phases in prescribed volume fractions f_1 and f_2 = 1 - f_1, where each phase i ∈ {1,2} has bulk modulus κ_i and shear modulus μ_i (with the limiting cases of one phase being rigid, μ_i = κ_i = ∞, or void, μ_i = κ_i = 0, allowed). For any such composite, the homogenized (effective) elasticity tensor is again isotropic and is characterized by an effective bulk modulus κ* and an effective shear modulus μ*. Define the attainable set

  G(f_1; κ_1, μ_1, κ_2, μ_2) = { (κ*, μ*) : (κ*, μ*) is realized by some isotropic two-phase composite with the given phase moduli and phase-1 volume fraction f_1 } ⊂ ℝ_{>0} × ℝ_{>0}.

The classical Hashin–Shtrikman–Walpole inequalities give two-sided bounds on κ* and μ* separately, and partial coupled bounds on the pair (κ*, μ*) are known.

Problem. Derive bounds on the set G(f_1; κ_1, μ_1, κ_2, μ_2) that strictly improve on the currently best-known inequalities relating κ* and μ* simultaneously, and ultimately determine the optimal (sharp, attainable) coupled bounds describing G exactly, including the cases in which one of the phases is rigid or void.
artifact.category_tag: Bounds on effective moduli of composites
artifact.status_search_result: While the separate Hashin–Shtrikman–Walpole bounds on κ* and μ* are classical and attainable in many regimes, the problem of finding optimal coupled bounds on the pair (κ*, μ*) for two-phase isotropic elastic composites remains open. Subsequent work (e.g., Cherkaev–Gibiansky, Milton, Allaire–Kohn, Liu) has produced partial improvements via translation/quasiconvexification methods and identified extremal microstructures attaining the bulk-modulus or shear-modulus bound separately, but a complete description of the optimal G-closure for two isotropic phases (especially with rigid or void inclusions) has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Bounds on the Effective Moduli of Composite Materials (Gibiansky lectures)
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes describing translation-method coupled (κ*,μ*) bounds for two-phase isotropic composites and noting that the complete G-closure is only partially known.
status_evidence.claim: Coupled (κ*,μ*) bounds beyond Hashin–Shtrikman are only partially established.

status_evidence.title: Hashin–Shtrikman bounds and their attainability for multiphase composites
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses attainability of HS bounds; full sharp coupled bounds for general two-phase isotropic elastic mixtures are not given.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp coupled elastic-moduli bounds for arbitrary two isotropic phases remain incompletely characterized.

status_evidence.title: A new class of extremal composites
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs microstructures attaining extremal bulk modulus, an ingredient toward but not a resolution of the optimal coupled (κ*,μ*) bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Progress exists on extremal microstructures, but the full optimal coupled bounds remain to be determined.
